historyTimeline.h2: Mitsubishi Outlander 2.0 (4B11) - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mitsubishi Outlander 2.0 4B11 arrived as a core petrol option in the second-generation Outlander (CW) from 2009, offering a reliable and efficient naturally aspirated alternative to the diesel variants that dominated UK fleet sales. The 4B11 continued into the third-generation Outlander (GG/ZJ/ZK) and formed the basis of the Outlander PHEV's petrol engine, making it one of the most widely fitted petrol units across the Outlander range.

milestones.description: 4B11 2.0L MIVEC petrol introduced on second-generation Outlander (CW), producing 148bhp
4B11 carried over into third-generation Outlander (GG/ZJ) as the entry-level petrol option
4B11 adapted for Outlander PHEV hybrid system, detuned to 118hp for generator duty
Facelift third-generation Outlander (ZK/ZM) retains 4B11 petrol variant alongside revised diesel and PHEV options
4B11 phased out in UK market as Mitsubishi shifted focus to PHEV and diesel

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Mitsubishi Outlander 2.0 4B11 is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

items.title: 2.0L Petrol MIVEC (2009-2018)
items.commonFailure: Accessory drive belt tensioner flange cracking is a known issue on 4B11 and 4B12 engines in Outlanders produced between 2008-2012, causing the drive belt to detach, battery discharge and potential engine stall - addressed by a manufacturer recall (SR-18-001) for belt tensioner replacement . Timing chain upper guide was eliminated on 4B11 engines from October 2009 onwards; replacement engine blocks may not have attachment holes for earlier-design guides . The 4B11 uses a timing chain rather than a belt, so no periodic timing belt replacement is required .

commonProblems.h2: Mitsubishi Outlander 2.0 (4B11) Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The 4B11 is generally robust for a modern petrol, but a few known wear points can lead to replacement decisions. The drive belt tensioner recall affects earlier Outlander 2.0 4B11 units, while timing chain guide elimination from late 2009 changes service procedure. Rebuilt 4B11 engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Drive Belt Tensioner Failure - Why the Mitsubishi Outlander 2.0 4B11 Tensioner Cracks
problems.rootCause: The automatic drive belt tensioner flange can crack, allowing the accessory drive belt to detach. This leads to battery discharge, loss of power steering and potential engine stall . The recall replaces the tensioner with an improved design.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace belt tensioner with improved design; fit new accessory belt
repairOptions.longevity: Ideal for Outlander 2.0 4B11 not yet recall-completed; low-cost insurance
Only if tensioner failure caused belt detachment and overheating/stall damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Mitsubishi Outlander 2.0 4B11 of relevant age (2009-2018) currently sits in the £5,000-£14,000 band [THIRD-PARTY]. Rebuilt supply at £2,500-£3,200 plus fitting sits at around 30-50% of vehicle value on mid-range examples, making replacement viable but worthy of careful evaluation. Older pre-2012 Outlander 2.0 values below £5,000 push replacement into Watch territory.
problems.recommendation: If your Outlander 2.0 4B11 is covered by the Mitsubishi recall SR-18-001, contact a dealer immediately for a free tensioner replacement - this is the most cost-effective approach. If the tensioner has already failed and caused belt detachment, assess whether stall damage affected the engine; if not, a simple belt-and-tensioner replacement is the right call. For engines with confirmed internal damage from overheating or stall, compare rebuilt and used engine prices - the 12-month warranty on a rebuilt unit often justifies the premium over a used engine of unknown history.

problems.affectedModels: Mitsubishi Outlander 2.0 4B11 built from October 2009 onwards

problems.recommendation: Listen for a cold-start rattle from the front of the engine - this is the primary warning sign of timing chain tensioner wear. If your Outlander 2.0 4B11 is pre-October 2009 production, budget for a full timing chain kit with the upper guide. For post-October 2009 engines, replacement is simpler and slightly cheaper. Stick to Mitsubishi-spec oil and logbook intervals - good lubrication is critical for timing chain longevity on 4B11 engines .

items.question: What are the signs of 4B11 engine failure in an Outlander 2.0?
items.answer: Common warning signs include a cold-start rattle from the timing chain area, loss of power or engine stall from drive belt detachment (especially if the belt tensioner recall SR-18-001 hasn't been completed), and excessive oil consumption.
keyPoints: Cold-start rattle -> timing chain tensioner or guide wear
Battery discharge warning + loss of power steering -> belt tensioner failure
Engine warning light -> investigate with diagnostic scan
items.cta: -> Need a 4B11 diagnosis? Get specialist quotes

items.question: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mitsubishi Outlander 2.0?
items.answer: A typical Outlander 2.0 4B11 from 2009-2018 is worth £5,000-£14,000, so a rebuilt engine at £2,500-£3,200 plus fitting often represents good value - around 30-50% of vehicle value. For pre-2012 Outlander 2.0 examples worth under £5,000, consider used engine options or evaluate scrap value.
keyPoints: Mid-range Outlander 2.0 (£6k-£10k): rebuilt engine is sensible if keeping the car 2+ years
Lower-value Outlander 2.0 (under £5k): used engine or repair typically makes more sense
High-value Outlander 2.0 (£12k+): replacement cost is small relative to value
items.cta: -> Compare your Outlander 2.0 engine replacement options

items.question: Does the Mitsubishi Outlander 2.0 (4B11) have a timing belt or chain?
items.answer: The 4B11 engine uses a timing chain, not a belt. That means no scheduled timing belt replacement interval - the chain is designed to last the life of the engine under normal conditions with proper oil maintenance .
keyPoints: No timing belt replacement required on Outlander 2.0 4B11
Keep up oil changes - chain, guides and tensioner rely on good lubrication
Listen for cold-start rattle; that's the primary timing chain warning sign
items.cta: -> Check your Outlander 2.0 4B11 timing chain health

items.question: What's the difference between the Outlander 2.0 4B11 and the 2.4 4B12?
items.answer: Both are from the same 4B1 engine family, sharing a timing chain design and MIVEC variable valve timing. The 4B12 is a 2.4L version (2,360cc) producing approximately 170bhp, while the 4B11 is 2.0L (1,997cc) at 148-150bhp. The 4B12 was offered in some markets as a higher-output petrol option but was less common in UK Outlander sales than the 4B11.
keyPoints: Both share MIVEC, timing chain, similar reliability profile
